prize_parts.citation: For the prediction of flat bands at a magic twist angle and the experimental discovery of correlated insulating and superconducting states in twisted bilayer graphene, opening the field of moire quantum matter

statement.case_for: Magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene is a discovery in nature rather than a formal construction: a precise 2011 prediction by Bistritzer and MacDonald that a single geometric parameter, the twist angle, quenches kinetic energy into flat bands, followed by the 2018 observation by Jarillo-Herrero's group of correlated insulators and superconductivity at exactly that angle. The prediction-then-discovery structure is the cleanest theory-plus-experiment story on the list, and the result seeded a large independent field (moire quantum matter, fractional Chern insulators, transition-metal dichalcogenide moire systems) replicated by many groups in about seven years. The core phenomenology is stable and the topic is genuinely new rather than a continuation of an already rewarded theme.
statement.case_against: The strongest reservation is maturity and attribution. The microscopic origin of the superconductivity and of several correlated phases is still debated, so a citation must be drafted around the robust facts (flat bands, correlated states, tunability) rather than a settled mechanism. The credited trio also omits the first experimental author of the key 2018 papers and other groups (Dean, Young, Yazdani, Kim) who made early confirmations, and Bistritzer's role relative to MacDonald's is a judgment call. Meanwhile B024 is a more mature and more cleanly attributed two-person case with broad support, so my preference for B003 is not self-evident.

responses.point: Ranked twisted bilayer graphene fourth and argued that the interpretation is not yet stable because the origin of the superconductivity and many correlated phases is still debated, so recognition could be somewhat early.
responses.response: I accept the premise but not the conclusion. The committee has historically rewarded the discovery of a phenomenon before its mechanism is understood; high-temperature superconductors are the obvious precedent. What must be stable is the observation and its reproducibility, and that is secure, with many independent groups seeing the correlated insulators and superconducting domes at the magic angle. I would therefore write the citation around flat bands and correlated states and avoid any statement on pairing. Where I do agree with Kroll is that this raises the bar for how carefully we phrase the citation, and I would be uneasy if the committee chose B003 while claiming more than we know.

responses.point: Ranked optical lattice clocks first as a clean two-person invention with confirmed 1e-18 performance, a natural successor to the 2005 frequency-comb prize, and ranked twisted bilayer graphene sixth as possibly somewhat early.
responses.response: Johansson makes the strongest case for B024 and I take it seriously: the attribution to Katori and Ye is compact, the replication across national laboratories is direct, and the redefinition of the second gives it a timely hook. My reservation is not about quality but about kind. The clock is an exceptionally refined invention that sharpens a measurement we already knew how to make, whereas twisted bilayer graphene revealed a state of matter nobody expected from a clean carbon system. I do not think four first places settle that question; they show where the instrument and measurement specialists on the committee cluster. I would rank B024 as the safe and defensible alternative, and I would not oppose it if the discussion converges there.

responses.point: Ranked Car-Parrinello ab initio molecular dynamics first, as an unambiguous two-person attribution that is four decades old, in near-universal use and arguably overdue.
responses.response: Eriksson is right that attribution and maturity are as good as anywhere on the list, and the method has plainly reshaped computational materials science. My hesitation is that the prize is for a discovery, and Car-Parrinello is a methodological invention that builds on density-functional theory already honoured in 1998; I would ask whether a committee wants to reward a tool whose scientific payoff is spread across chemistry and materials rather than one identifiable result. It also received support from only two members, so I would not put it into the final configuration without a clearer argument that it is physics in the prize's sense.

responses.point: Ranked active matter and flocking first and noted that the Toner-Tu exponents have only limited quantitative confirmation, and also flagged the 2016 topological prize as an overlap problem for topological insulators.
responses.response: Mehlig's remark about the 2016 overlap is the right argument against B023, which is why I place it second to B003 only narrowly and as an alternative: the quantum spin Hall effect and the Z2 invariant are a conceptual landmark, but the committee would have to explain why a second topology prize is warranted so soon. By contrast, moire flat bands are not a classification of band topology but a new way of generating strong correlations, so the overlap is smaller. I also note that Mehlig himself ranked B003 third, which suggests support for it is broader than the first-place counts imply.

uncertainties: Whether the committee will accept a three-name credit that excludes the first experimental author (Yuan Cao) and other early experimental contributors, and whether a two-name prize (MacDonald and Jarillo-Herrero) would be fairer.
Whether the pairing mechanism of superconductivity in twisted graphene will be clarified enough to affect how the citation is phrased.
Whether the 2016 topological prize and the 2025 superconducting-circuit prize count against B023 and B043 more heavily than I assume.
statement.conflict_note: No specific conflict is apparent from my profile. My documented connections are professional (David Gross, Hector Rubinstein, Thomas Van Riet and the Uppsala theory group), and none of these people appears among the credited names on the shortlist.
